A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DistillGaze. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, Appendix A and Appendix B.1–B.7 are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Project Aria gaze-estimation experiments, teacher/student comparisons, qualitative predictions and ablations, including extended appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original gaze-estimation experiments and appendix analyses, including full Error-User tables and loss-component ablations.

M1.justification: The reported training objectives receive a limited refinement: Eqs. (8) and (13) replace separately specified loss weights with complementary weights, using 1 - lambda_SynSup and 1 - lambda_t. The architecture, constituent losses and inference procedure remain unchanged. This establishes a revised objective specification, without establishing an implementation change or experimental rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Project Aria near-eye gaze task, 2,222 real participants and synthetic dataset of 165K frames from 998 subjects. Neither adds another device configuration, dataset or evaluated deployment scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding main and appendix tables, including DARE-GRAM, pseudo-label-only distillation, SP, VIC-KD, Community KD and the supervised references. Sapiens2 is added only to related work, not evaluated.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 and Appendix A retain the same participant splits, preprocessing, model sizes, training budgets and evaluation procedures. Both sample 64 frames per recording, reserve nine for personalization, evaluate the remaining 55 and exclude gaze angles outside ±40 degrees.

E4.justification: The architecture, teacher-loss and loss-component/scheduler ablations are retained, as are the embedding analyses and qualitative cases. The third example in v2 Figure 4 comes from v1 Figure 10; it is relocated evidence, not an added case study.

E5.justification: Both versions report 95% confidence intervals from a hierarchical bootstrap over users and frames with 1,000 iterations. No repeated-run, seed or statistical-estimation practice changes are reported; revised interval values belong to E6.

E6.justification: Several numerical discrepancies are corrected. Table 1 changes the DINOv3 linear-probe parenthesized intervals from 0.63 to 0.61 for E75U75 and 1.71 to 1.60 for E90U90. Table 6 changes on-device DARE-GRAM E50U50 from 2.97 to 2.96 degrees and the supervised reference E90U90 from 5.90 to 5.91 degrees, alongside other interval corrections. Table 2 and DistillGaze's headline errors remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal objectives are revised: Eq. (8) supplies an explicit self-distillation sum over synthetic and real data, while Eq. (13) explicitly aggregates over real data; both specify complementary weighting relationships. These are limited mathematical-specification corrections. The remaining definitions and formulas are retained, with no added theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v2 strengthens the deployment claim by explicitly asserting a reduction in development time from months to days in the introduction and conclusion. v1 claims rapid iteration without that timeframe. The central two-stage contribution and accuracy claims remain, and no timing experiment accompanies the stronger claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds a substantive explanation of rapid adaptation through reusable eye assets, updated optical parameters and passive collection of target-device appearance statistics. The single-device and difficult-tail limitations remain. The teacher-quality explanation expanded in Section 5.3 already appeared in v1 Appendix B.4 and is not a new interpretation.

D1.justification: The revised loss equations explicitly identify aggregation domains and relationships between weights, reducing ambiguity in the training recipe. Section 3.2 also explicitly names the backbone, projector and gaze head as EMA-updated components. Hardware, optimizer, augmentation, training budgets and resource-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 adds Sapiens2 and a brief description of its human-centric pretraining. The earlier cited works and positioning around DINOv3, synthetic-to-real adaptation and Community KD are otherwise retained; extensive reference renumbering is bibliographic presentation.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, methods and results undergo extensive sentence and paragraph rewriting. v2 expands deployment motivation and clarifies the different teacher/student roles across stages while retaining the overall section sequence. The language revision extends well beyond isolated corrections.

P2.justification: The document receives a substantially different typesetting scheme with narrower text blocks, running headers and restyled captions and tables. Figures 1 and 2 are redesigned, plot labels and legends are adjusted, and one qualitative example moves from Figure 10 to Figure 4. These are extensive visual changes despite largely retained evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity and internal consistency through clearer stage-specific explanations, more explicit loss specifications and corrections to several main-text/appendix numerical discrepancies and captions. The empirical support is essentially unchanged. The new, unmeasured months-to-days deployment claim overstates the demonstrated evidence and limits the net improvement.
